ui.note: Text people type keeps its own direction in Arabic: input and textarea fields use dir=auto, rendered notes and comments take their own direction, and titles, list and people names and label chips inside translated text are isolated so punctuation and list separators stay in place. Arabic link underlines use a larger offset. Behavior, permissions, data and keyboard shortcuts are unchanged. Attachment uploads and archive import explain retained deleted bytes and restore windows in all six languages; the file menu preserves writable uploaders' own deletion rights. Avatar rendering rejects foreign URLs in every member view and uses initials instead. Browser token refresh refuses missing or mismatched subjects and enters the existing sign-in-required state without reconnecting another account.

release.note: Document environment secrets, the Compose release default and the version synchronization command.

configuration.note: Document the released Compose image default and the explicit nightly selection. The auth and all-in-one URL settings accept HTTP(S) origins without credentials, paths, queries or fragments and normalize trailing slashes. Empty auth settings fall back to the public URL. Other settings retain their meanings.

deployment.note: Record the deployed Compose image tag for recovery; the default now follows the released version and image packages, including musl, are pinned. The all-in-one wrapper validates public URLs as origins and normalizes trailing slashes. Remove paths, queries and fragments before upgrading. No image topology, credential format or storage migration changes.

native.noImpact: Refuse Capacitor file, content and HTTP proxy resources for every WebView request, clear exported Activity task affinity and explicitly exclude native session and push preferences from Android cloud backup and device transfer. Preserve the release-only manifest guard and trusted-server choice of HTTPS sync origin. Source/build checks do not qualify Android runtime behavior. Native sync follows the bundled Zero 1.11.1 client: Android and desktop accept exactly /sync/v53/connect on the configured Zero origin (was v51, so beta.1 native apps never opened a sync socket) and relay inbound binary poke chunks up to 1 MiB to the page as base64, rebuilt as ArrayBuffers; malformed frames end the socket, an oversized frame gives the page one abnormal close before any later frame, and the page still sends text frames only. A pin test reads the installed Zero client and fails when either native path or inbound bound drifts. Grant, session, JWT splicing, refusal fences and canonical HTTPS checks are unchanged; no migration, storage or server change. The shared migration response parser also preserves optional retained-deleted quota details for browser feedback; native request, bridge and ciphertext formats remain compatible. Require a verified current native session before dispatching file, archive export or E2E bridge operations. Restored vault credentials alone cannot authorize them before session.read. Existing offline proof, request-fence recovery, captured ownership and private saved-file permissions remain unchanged. Unit and web checks do not qualify installed native runtime behavior.

authentication.noImpact: Preserve the Better Auth 1.7.12 upgrade, JWT/provider-account migrations, explicit provider linking, nonce validation, verified-email admission and scoped Apple origin checks. Reset atomically consumes its token, writes the password, verifies the mailbox and retires sessions, native authority, access tokens, feeds, passkeys, provider links and pending account proofs while retaining TOTP and backup codes. Enforce the enrolled local factor on every sign-in path, including social/OIDC/SAML callbacks, passkeys and native system-browser flows. Reuse the plugin challenge, provisional-session deletion and reset invalidation. Provider MFA and remembered-device cookies cannot substitute. Native grants retain their ID and stay unapproved until successful factor completion and explicit consent; no bridge permissions or credential formats change. Upgrade server/web together and reload sign-in pages; rollback loses this protection. The password credential remains linked so password-protected account settings keep their password requirement. Other provider accounts can still be unlinked. No credential format or native handoff changes. Password changes retain passkeys and provider links while retiring other sessions, access tokens, feeds and pending proofs transactionally, replacing the initiating cookie without returning its token and leaving email verification unchanged. SAML requires browser-bound RelayState unless IdP-initiated sign-in is enabled. Bootstrap counts soft-deleted accounts; auth requires a configured origin in production. E2E rate limits require test mode; detached reset mail uses a hashed recipient budget without changing responses. No storage or native bridge changes. The native portability factory forwards attachment storage limits to the shared migration handlers. Bearer validation, sessions, route guards, admission, credentials and native bridge permissions are unchanged.

compatibility.note: Migration 0092 binds membership-key inserts to the recipient membership and caller granter, restricts wrap and request updates to their writer columns, and guards broad custom grants with triggers. Existing non-superuser roles with DELETE on focus_interval_start retain pruning execution automatically. Startup reports privileged attributes, memberships, RLS ownership and missing cleanup execution; pruning errors do not stop reminder scanning. Deployment logins and Zero publications are unchanged. Migration 0091 adds nullable habit_log.completed_by referencing the user with ON DELETE SET NULL. Existing logs remain unattributed. Direct and reminder completion derive the actor from authenticated context; duplicate ticks preserve the original attribution and Karma award. Membership removal preserves attribution; account deletion explicitly clears the actor while preserving the occurrence and anonymized user row. The actor index and validated foreign key match the generated schema. Attachment transfers claim an exclusive upload token and unique storage key, release the pooled client during streaming, then relock and revalidate before recording bytes and hash. Finalize refuses an unfinished transfer; canceled or retired transfers cannot publish over a replacement. Transfer errors retain retryable reservations, identical thumbnail retries succeed, and expiring transfer leases fence stalled writers. Migration reserve/recover uses the configured attachment quota and combined file limit, and returns 404 when E2E is disabled. Retained deleting rows consume quota, writable uploaders retain their own deletion right, and recipients discard rejected grants before requesting replacements. Quota refusals report retained bytes and the latest restore window, with localized feedback; migration 0094 adds nullable attachment.gc_retry_at that records GC failure backoff and sweeps summarize progress. Browser token subjects must match the captured account.
compatibility.upgrade: Stop app and Zero writers, back up the coordinated recovery set, and apply 0092 using the migration owner. Existing non-superuser runtime roles with DELETE on focus_interval_start receive cleanup execution during migration, including custom names. Newly created roles or roles without that prior privilege need the documented explicit grant before deployment. Check provider-admin memberships before upgrading. Stop application and Zero writers, back up the coordinated recovery set, and apply migration 0093 with the migration role before starting the updated server. Existing rows need no backfill. Back up the coordinated recovery set, stop app and Zero writers and apply migration 0091 with the migration role before starting the updated app and Zero. No backfill or role-policy change is required. Upgrade web and native server routes together after the coordinated backup and apply migration 0094 (attachment GC retry) before serving traffic; no ciphertext conversion is required. Reload web clients to enforce the captured-account token check. Native host credential storage and its existing update procedure are unchanged.
compatibility.backup: Preserve the existing coordinated PostgreSQL, encrypted attachment, replica and original-secret recovery set. No encrypted-data conversion or row rewrite occurs. Preserve server-only upload tokens and opaque storage keys in PostgreSQL backups together with the matching attachment snapshot and original key envelopes. Include habit logs and their nullable attribution in the regular coordinated PostgreSQL recovery set, with the existing attachment ciphertext and secrets. Retain GC retry timestamps with database rows; retained deleting rows stay quota-bearing until GC, and a rejected grant removes only the recipient wrap for that request version. Existing coordinated database, attachment and secret backups remain sufficient because this change creates no new persistent format or migration.
compatibility.rollback: Keep the migration, column grants and function ACL when rolling back the app; the preceding writers use the same wrap and fulfilment columns and pruning function. Restoring the coordinated backup discards newer changes. Stop writers, retain the additive nullable column and let unfinished reservations expire before accepting uploads on the preceding server. A database rollback requires a matching coordinated backup and loses later writes. Retain the additive nullable column, index and foreign key when running the preceding app. Before upgrading again, stop writers and clear completed_by on all logs to remove stale attribution from the rollback window. A pre-upgrade backup restore discards later completions. Retain the additive nullable GC retry column when rolling back the app; preceding servers restore prior accounting and deletion rules, and discarded wraps need a new request or coordinated backup. Reverting the client removes the additional subject and avatar checks; no database or credential conversion is required for rollback.
compatibility.clientVersions: Existing browser and native clients remain compatible; no client schema or storage format changes. Web and native clients retain the same upload, finalize and ciphertext formats. Existing client versions remain compatible without an update. Reload browser clients and update native clients to display attribution. Existing clients retain one shared tick per habit per day, and the updated server sets the caller even for older completion requests. Existing attachment request and ciphertext formats remain compatible; reload browser clients to display retained-quota explanations and the uploader deletion menu. Browser token acquisition now takes the captured account ID and checks the returned JWT subject. Native runtimes continue using opaque vault-owned handles; no persisted replica, credential or protocol format changes. Updated browser clients reject refresh tokens for another account. Existing native runtimes retain their opaque handles and named operation boundary.

clients.note: Ship CLI/MCP/TUI JavaScript bundles for user-installed Bun 1.3.14+; document archive/checksum verification, MCP launch, JSON --version, BUILDINFO building-Bun identity, source URLs and notices/license texts covering every bundled or dependency-inlined package. The shebang uses --no-env-file and --config=/dev/null to prevent working-directory environment/preload injection. Minimum-version failure exits 2 and suffixes are tolerated. Scope is any Bun OS, qualified on Linux x64; rebuilds name tagged commit, building Bun and GNU tar. Commands, API envelopes, other exit codes and environment credentials remain unchanged. Standalone binary publication remains blocked/deferred. CLI output escapes terminal C1 and bidirectional controls while preserving decoded JSON values. MCP write tools are disabled until the fixed startup environment sets DITERO_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=1; direct calls cannot bypass SDK disabling. Existing credentials, membership checks, strict schemas and idempotency rules remain authoritative.

public-api.note: Preserve minute, second and fractional-second ISO timestamp acceptance for task create/update/completion, observations and metadata. Offset-capable inputs retain explicit offsets or Z; UTC-only responses remain UTC-only. CSV retains acceptance and normalization. No API version or persisted format changes. Reject dot-segment identifiers in the shared public API ID schema so CLI and MCP workflows cannot normalize into another endpoint. Document redaction of calendar-feed capability segments in proxy, access and telemetry logs. No migration, stored format, mutator or API envelope changes.
